newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway debt firms,trade quiet ahead of CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Norway debt firms,trade quiet ahead of CPI data.

text.p: Norwegian bonds firmed as buying interest came back into the market and yield spreads against German Bunds narrowed across most maturities, dealers said.
"We outperformed Germany early in the morning and closed the gap (with Bunds) for the 10-year by two to three points very quickly," said one dealer.
"The main reason is the slightly firmer crown, but some investors thought things were overdone yesterday and the spread was too wide. They came in on the buying side today."
At 1400 GMT, the crown was at 4.0470 against the mark and at 99.25 on the inverse European Currency Unit index.
The yield spread for the 2007 bond moved out to 38 points at one stage on Tuesday as the Norwegian market languished behind Germany. It stood around 37 points at yesterday's close.
Dealers said the yield curve for Norwegian debt was holding steady at around 210 basis points between the two-year and 10-year bonds.
But activity was thin with many players opting to stay out of the market before Thursday's domestic consumer price figures for March.
Ten analysts polled by Reuters forecast a month-on-month increase of 0.35 percent and for inflation to rise by 3.15 percent from March, 1996.
